clue.text: Tired, plump guide stumbled

parts.note: plump means fat, well rounded

indicators.note: stumbled suggests the letters of guide tripping into a new order

explanation.surface: A tubby tour guide trips over, worn out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plump' looks like an adjective for the guide, but it supplies its own piece; 'stumbled' is the anagram signal for the guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Being tired is the same as being weary or worn out, which is that sense.

clue.text: It's the talk of Paris

parts.note: not gossip in Paris but the language spoken there

explanation.walkthrough: 'the talk of' suggests something everyone is discussing; here talk means language.
explanation.definitionFit: Parisians speak the national language of France.

clue.text: Number try hit with difficulty

indicators.note: with difficulty suggests the letters of try hit being forced awkwardly into a new order

explanation.surface: A number of attempts to hit, all difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with difficulty' rearranges TRYHIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Three times ten is this figure.

clue.text: Diving bird upends huge mass of ice with energy

indicators.note: upends turns the word for the ice mass on its head, so in a down entry it reads bottom to top

parts.note: a berg is an iceberg, a huge mass of ice
E is the abbreviation for energy in physics

explanation.surface: A diving bird energetically tips over an iceberg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upends' suits a down entry: the iceberg word is read from bottom to top.
explanation.definitionFit: A water bird that dives for fish, known for elaborate courtship displays.

clue.text: Exclude king in extract

indicators.note: in says the king's letter goes inside the word for exclude

parts.note: to except is to exclude or leave out
R is the abbreviation for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Leave the monarch out of the passage.
explanation.definitionFit: A short passage taken from a book or film is an extract.

clue.text: Puffer inside the carriage!

explanation.surface: A smoker is found in a railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Old British trains had separate compartments where tobacco was allowed, called by the same name as the person puffing away.
explanation.definitionFit: A puffer is someone who smokes a pipe or cigarette; and a railway carriage set aside for tobacco users was known by the same word.

clue.text: Cloud of other materials

indicators.note: other suggests a different arrangement of the letters of materials

explanation.surface: A cloud made of different fabrics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'other' rearranges MATERIALS; 'of' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Long wispy cirrus streaks in the sky are named after a horse's tail.

clue.text: Continue to look after a bird

parts.note: to keep an animal is to look after it
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: Keep caring for a feathered friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To persist or carry on with an effort is to persevere.

clue.text: Jack held by left-wing newsman was delayed

indicators.note: held by says the sailor's word sits inside the left-wing word

parts.note: red means left-wing, socialist
a jack tar, or just tar, is a sailor
ED is short for editor, a newsman

explanation.surface: A sailor taken in by a left-wing journalist was held up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' is a sailor here, from jack tar, not a playing card or a lifting tool; 'held by' signals the container.
explanation.definitionFit: To be held back or slowed is to be delayed.

clue.text: Cardinal point?

parts.note: not a compass direction but a churchman's title of honour, also meaning a high point of ground

explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal point' looks like north, south, east or west; a cardinal is addressed as His Eminence, and the word also means a raised piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardinal's style of address is His Eminence, and the word also means a prominent rise or high point.

clue.text: Serviceman?

parts.note: not a soldier or sailor but a man who conducts church services

explanation.walkthrough: 'Serviceman' suggests the armed forces; here the service is a church one.
explanation.definitionFit: A clergyman leads religious services, so he is a man of the service in that sense.

clue.text: Unending elegy turned into a song a joy

indicators.note: turned into says the shortened letters are converted into a new arrangement
unending says the last letter of elegy is cut away

explanation.surface: A sad poem, never finished, becomes a happy song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unending' drops Y from ELEGY, and 'turned into' rearranges ELEG.
explanation.definitionFit: A part-song for unaccompanied voices has this name, and the word also means delight or merriment.

clue.text: The most important building to see

definitions.text: The most important building to see

parts.words: The most important building to see
parts.note: a 'see' is a bishop's diocese, and its principal church is the main building in it

explanation.walkthrough: 'to see' reads like sightseeing advice, but a see is a bishop's diocese, whose chief church holds his throne.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal church of a diocese, holding the bishop's throne, is the chief building of that see.

clue.text: Flight member's fixed gaze, one hears

indicators.note: one hears signals that the word for a fixed gaze is to be taken as heard, giving a word with the same sound

parts.note: a fixed gaze is a stare

explanation.surface: An airline crew member's fixed gaze, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight member' suggests aircrew; the flight is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight of steps is made up of individual steps, each one part of that staircase.

clue.text: This way to become an outsider

definitions.text: This way to become an outsider

parts.words: This way to become an outsider
parts.note: a sign reading 'this way' points to the door by which you leave and end up outside

explanation.walkthrough: 'outsider' suggests a social misfit, but here it is just someone who has gone out of the building.
explanation.definitionFit: The way out of a building is the door that takes you outdoors, as the sign above it says.

clue.text: Instrument that gets hammered

parts.note: a percussion instrument played by striking wooden bars with small mallets

explanation.walkthrough: 'gets hammered' hints at drunkenness or damage; it is just played with hammers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wooden bars struck with mallets make this percussion instrument.

clue.text: Take a look at the abandoned diggings

parts.note: abandoned means former, no longer in use, which is ex
the stands in for an indefinite article, a
diggings are a mine, where minerals are dug

explanation.surface: Go and inspect the disused mine workings.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'an ex-mine', a former mine, when split up.
explanation.definitionFit: To take a look at something is to inspect or scrutinise it.

clue.text: Putting on a bandage

explanation.surface: Applying a bandage to a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting clothes on is getting clad; and a covering for a wound is also called by this word.

clue.text: Result of having too much of what the doctor ordered?

definitions.text: Result of having too much of what the doctor ordered?

parts.words: Result of having too much of what the doctor ordered?
parts.note: the phrase 'just what the doctor ordered' means something good; too much medicine is a danger

explanation.walkthrough: Plays on 'just what the doctor ordered': taking too much of a prescribed drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking an excessive quantity of a medicine is this.

clue.text: Go round with a sawn-off gun

indicators.note: sawn-off says the gun's word has its end cut away, like a shortened barrel

parts.note: a revolver is a type of handgun

explanation.surface: Walk around armed with a sawn-off shotgun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sawn-off' removes the final R of REVOLVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To go round is to rotate or turn about an axis.

clue.text: Catch sight of agent on the end ofthe line

indicators.note: the end of the line picks out its final letter

parts.note: an agent is a spy

explanation.surface: Spot a secret agent at the far end of the phone line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ofthe' is the printed run-together form of 'of the'. E from line joins SPY.
explanation.definitionFit: To espy is to glimpse or notice.

clue.text: Cunning as little William losing a pound

indicators.note: losing says the pound's letter drops out of the name

parts.note: Willy is a pet form of William
L is the abbreviation for a pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Cunning as a young boy who has lost a pound coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' takes one L out of WILLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Being cunning means being crafty and sly.

clue.text: Summons a number have inscribed

parts.note: a writ is a court summons
ten is a number

explanation.surface: Court summonses, several of them, have been written up.
explanation.definitionFit: Words that are inscribed are set down on paper or stone.

clue.text: Save the engineers' signal

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, the British army corps
a cue is a signal to begin

explanation.surface: Save the army engineers' call to act.
explanation.definitionFit: To save someone from danger is to deliver them.

clue.text: Very large flag of an ancient Egyptian god

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, very large in clothing
a flag is an iris, the flower

explanation.surface: The huge banner of a god of old Egypt.
explanation.walkthrough: A flag is a yellow iris, the plant, not a banner.
explanation.definitionFit: The god of the dead and the underworld in Egyptian myth.

clue.text: The way to hit with a leather band

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
to rap is to hit sharply

explanation.surface: This is how to strike someone with a belt.
explanation.definitionFit: A thong or belt of leather for fastening is this.

clue.text: Trying to write with such a pen oil would be

definitions.text: Trying to write with such a pen oil would be

parts.words: Trying to write with such a pen oil would be
parts.note: a pen without a nib cannot write, so any attempt would be futile

explanation.walkthrough: The pen lacks a tip, so attempting to write with it is useless.
explanation.definitionFit: Futile effort is useless, and a pen lacking its tip makes writing exactly that.

clue.text: In diplomacy I stay silent

indicators.note: In says the I sits inside the word for diplomacy

parts.note: tact is diplomacy

explanation.surface: Being diplomatic, I keep quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside TACT; 'stay' links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something understood without being spoken is unspoken.

clue.text: Is there nothing on the shell of a crustacean?

indicators.note: on says the pieces before it sit next to the shell's word in the across entry

parts.note: taken as written
nothing is zero, the letter O
a pod is the shell or husk of peas or beans

explanation.surface: Is there nothing inside a crustacean's shell?
explanation.definitionFit: A woodlouse or similar small crustacean with a flat body belongs to this order.

clue.text: Banger in the showroom?

parts.note: a banger is British slang for an old car; one in a dealer's showroom is a car in stock

explanation.walkthrough: A banger is British slang for a battered old car; such cars are raced in crash-prone stock car racing, and a car in the showroom is one in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Old cars used for racing are called this, and a car held for sale is in stock.

clue.text: Let Reg become a fairy-tale character

indicators.note: become asks the letters of Let Reg to turn into something else

explanation.surface: Allow Reg to be cast as a figure in a children's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'become' rearranges LETREG.
explanation.definitionFit: Hansel's sister in the Grimm story of the gingerbread house.

clue.text: Needlewomen's fancy trinkets

indicators.note: fancy as a verb or adjective suggests imaginative reworking of the letters of trinkets

explanation.surface: Seamstresses are trinkets you might take a liking to.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is', linking definition and wordplay; 'fancy' rearranges TRINKETS.
explanation.definitionFit: Women who work with needles and wool, making jumpers and scarves.
